name: CANGAROO
full_name: Collaboration of Australia and Nippon for a GAmma Ray Observatory in the Outback
summary: Historical Japanese–Australian Cherenkov-telescope series whose Galactic-center observations tested cold-dark-matter radiation.
detection_principle: Single and later multiple telescopes image atmospheric Cherenkov light to reconstruct very-high-energy gamma-ray spectra.

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: ICRR's official history explicitly states that the project ended on 2012-03-31.

collaboration.name: CANGAROO collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

phases.name: CANGAROO-II
phases.description: Single 7 m telescope upgraded to 10 m

results.summary: Galactic-center observations constrained specific cold-dark-matter-halo scenarios; not a dark-matter discovery.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
